title: Upper density vanishes a.e. on a ψ-null closed set with uniform upper bound
statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, k := m+1, ψ an outer measure on ℝᵏ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), K ⊆ ℝᵏ closed with ψ(K) = 0, C ∈ [0,∞) and r > 0 such that ψ(B(z,τ)) ≤ C·τᵏ for all z ∈ K and all 0 < τ < r (B open balls, τᵏ = ENNReal.ofReal(τᵏ)). Then for Lᵏ-almost every c ∈ K, i.e. for (Lᵏ restricted to K)-a.e. c, limsup_{t↓0} ψ(B(c,t))/tᵏ = 0, the limsup being taken along 𝓝[>]0 in [0,∞].
lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (ψ : OuterMeasure (Eucl (m + 1))) (K : Set (Eucl (m + 1))) (C : ℝ≥0∞) (r : ℝ), IsClosed K → ψ K = 0 → C ≠ ⊤ → 0 < r → (∀ z ∈ K, ∀ τ ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) r, ψ (ball z τ) ≤ C * ENNReal.ofReal (τ ^ (m + 1))) → ∀ᵐ c ∂((volume : Measure (Eucl (m + 1))).restrict K), limsup (fun t : ℝ => ψ (ball c t) / ENNReal.ofReal (t ^ (m + 1))) (𝓝[>] 0) = 0
